clue.text: Unofficially, leave starts with it

parts.note: starts as a verb, jerks in surprise, means jumps
being with it, fashionable, means being hip

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out that taking leave begins with something unofficial.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump ship is to desert a post without permission, leaving unofficially.

clue.text: Rise and fall in tune with dual arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of music reorders things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement of a tune for two voices rises and falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To undulate is to move in waves, rising and falling smoothly.

clue.text: Fancy including empty line in forecast

indicators.note: including means one word holds the other inside

parts.note: a forecast is a prediction

indicators.note: empty means the word line loses its contents, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An elaborate forecast with a blank line in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A predilection is a liking or preference, as is a fancy for something.

clue.text: Around a wet resort have unusually warm spell

indicators.note: around means the word have wraps the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, means the letters are sorted again

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers at a rainy seaside resort enjoy an unseasonably hot spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but is read as re-sort, the anagram signal; 'Around' has the second word wrap the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A heatwave is a period of unusually hot weather.

clue.text: Call my number, and there's a distinctive sound

parts.note: to call someone is to phone them
my reads as me, the speaker

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be rung, mentioning a distinctive ringtone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' simply completes the phrase 'Call my number', a request to ring the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoneme is a distinct unit of sound in a language that separates one word from another.

clue.text: Pays for doctors

definitions.meaning: someone who stands a round pays for others
medics attending patients give them medical care

explanation.definitionFit: To treat is both to buy something for another person and to give medical care.

clue.text: Distinctive quality, useless if pronounced

indicators.note: pronounced means the word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: vain means useless, as in a vain attempt

explanation.surface: A remark that a distinctive trait is pointless if spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein is a streak or strain of character, as in a vein of humour.

clue.text: Gloss over blue end to stage show

indicators.note: end to means the second word is placed at the end of the first

parts.note: a play is a stage show
blue means sad, down

explanation.surface: Someone smooths over a risqué finale to a theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: To play down something is to minimise it, which glossing over also does.

clue.text: Having to rush, scientist makes bloomer

parts.note: to rush, run fast, is to hare
Alexander Graham Bell, the scientist credited with the telephone

explanation.surface: A hurried scientist commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A harebell is a wild flower, and a bloomer is a plant that flowers.

clue.text: One cuts commercials on radio

indicators.note: something on the radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: commercials are advertisements, ads

explanation.surface: A broadcaster trims the advertising breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a woodworking tool with an arched blade, so it is something that cuts.

clue.text: Where to find partner one left dancing with gaiety when drunk?

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters reeling about into a new arrangement
one left means the letter standing for one departs from the word dancing

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A single person left alone on the dance floor, merry and tipsy, wonders where to find a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes I out of DANCING to leave DANCNG; that and GAIETY are rearranged ('when drunk').
explanation.definitionFit: A dating agency is a business that matches people looking for a romantic partner.

clue.text: Desperately need a good (short) clue 'for perfume

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: short means the word good loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver pleads for a decent clue to a perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a light scented water, a kind of perfume.

clue.text: In bed, root of trouble had returned

indicators.note: returned means the letters come back in the opposite order

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, the cause of trouble
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sickly patient in bed, where the trouble began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the whole two-word run around. The definition is cryptic: a flower is something found in a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden flower commonly grown in beds, so it is something found in a bed.

clue.text: Fly low having nobody on board

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make
a squit is an insignificant person, a nobody (British slang)

explanation.surface: A plane flying low with no passengers aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' and 'low' look like flying; MOO (low, as cattle do) holds SQUIT, British slang for a nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito is an insect of the fly order, a gnat-like biting fly.

clue.text: Fail initially to cut cost

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Fail

parts.note: to etch is to cut a design into a surface

explanation.surface: Advice about cutting spending.
explanation.definitionFit: An item that fetched a price was sold for it, so the past tense of fetch can mean cost.

clue.text: Bird may be flipping duck

parts.note: flipping and flaming are both mild British intensifiers, euphemisms for stronger swear words
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, O

explanation.surface: Exasperated remark that a bird may be a blasted duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like turning over; it is a mild British oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a tall pink wading bird.

clue.text: Make fresh reports about aid for drivers reversing

indicators.note: reversing means the whole construction is read backwards
about means one word wraps round the other

parts.note: reports are news
a golf tee helps players hitting with drivers

explanation.surface: Fresh reports on help for motorists who are backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the golf aid inside the reports, and 'reversing' turns the result round to give NETEEWS backwards. The drivers are golf clubs, not motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten something is to freshen it, as when sweetening stale air or breath.

clue.text: Start to worry computer crime may become enormous

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word worry

parts.note: hacking is breaking into computer systems illegally

explanation.surface: A warning that a small worry about cybercrime may grow huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacking is British informal for very large, as in a whacking great bill.

clue.text: Truck with florins and sixpences could one say?

definitions.meaning: truck as a noun means trade or dealings, as in having no truck with

definitions.text: florins and sixpences could one say?
definitions.meaning: florins and sixpences were British coins withdrawn at decimalisation, so they are former small coins

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as EX (former) plus CHANGE (coins); florins and sixpences were pre-1971 British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchange means trade, as truck does; ex-change is playful for former coinage.

clue.text: Turned out dry — got warm and fresh outside

indicators.note: outside means the first word goes round the other

parts.note: laundry that is aired has been warmed and freshened
TT, teetotal, means dry, not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: Laundry hung outside becomes dry, warm and fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' means dressed, as in well turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well turned out is smartly dressed, that is, attired.

clue.text: Fortune or disaster

definitions.meaning: chance or luck, as in meeting by ...

explanation.definitionFit: An accident is both a chance happening and a damaging mishap.

clue.text: Trick bridge player comes up with right away

indicators.note: comes up, in a down clue, means the letters read from bottom to top
away means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: in bridge each player has a partner across the table

explanation.surface: A bridge player pulls off a trick straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTNER without R gives PARTNE; 'comes up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to trick them into a trap.

clue.text: Bring Conservative leader in to make amends right away

indicators.note: bring in means put inside the other word

parts.note: to atone is to make amends

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of Conservative

explanation.surface: A political call to bring the Tory leader in to apologise immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: At once is a common idiom meaning immediately, without delay.

clue.text: Transformed into kind host? No way

indicators.note: transformed means the letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether a guest could be turned into a kindly host replies doubtfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal phrases of refusal or disbelief, the idiom used to say firmly not.

clue.text: Loose turf almost upset old lines man

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the letters run the other way
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a divot is a piece of turf torn up, as by a golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer's loose divot unsettles an old liar.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVOT less its last letter is DIVO; 'upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet, an ancient writer of lines of verse.

clue.text: Mob recorded by recording angel

indicators.note: recorded by means the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: A heavenly recording angel writes down the misdeeds of a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of people acting together, like a mob or crowd.

clue.text: Slide one's son found in open space in wood

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: a glade is a clearing in a wood
one is I, and one's stands for one is, IS
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A boy slips over in a woodland clearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is': I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissade is a sliding movement, in ballet or a controlled slide down snow.

clue.text: Harry set to accept royal title? Nonsense

parts.note: to harry is to dog, pursue persistently

indicators.note: to accept means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: to set, as jelly does, is to gel
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's title

explanation.surface: Prince Harry seems ready to take a royal title, which is called nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is badly written comic verse, worthless writing amounting to nonsense.
